summary: Given the open-ended "build a notifications system" request, Claude Code immediately loaded the brainstorming skill, classified the work as architectural, asked five rounds of clarifying questions (starting point, single vs multi-user, triggers, delivery, stack/durability), and then presented a sectioned design with no implementation code written.
reasoning: All three criteria are supported by the session log and the screen transcript: brainstorming skill loaded as the very first tool call, five clarifying-question rounds, a concrete design direction produced, and zero implementation files written (workdir unchanged). The only oddity is the skill's plugin namespace being `hyperpowers` rather than `superpowers` as the story states.

observations.description: Acceptance criterion names the skill `superpowers:brainstorming`, but the session log records `hyperpowers:brainstorming`. Functionally equivalent here, but the naming mismatch between story/fixture and product could break automated checks.

The multi-select question ("Triggers") required 4 Down presses past the options to reach Submit, then a second confirmation screen ("Ready to submit your answers?"). Slightly heavy for a two-checkbox answer.

Agent re-framed the feature from "notifications" to "reminders" and recommended single-user before the user had expressed any opinion. Well-argued and it offered 'Still not sure' as an option, but a less attentive user could be steered past the original request's multi-user premise.

Design is presented in sections with "I'll pause after each" — a reasonable pattern, but each pause requires a free-text reply rather than an approve/revise prompt, so it's less obvious than the earlier structured questions that input is expected.
First design section took "Cogitated for 2m 17s"; the screen was static during that time (log was the only sign of progress).

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification first: architectural ... this isn't a bounded change to an existing flow; it's new structure, and it gets the full treatment: questions → approaches → design → spec → plan. No code until you approve a design." Workdir still contains only index.html (`ls -la` + `git status --short` in coding-agent-workdir returned clean, single file).

criteria.criterion: Brainstorming skill invoked before any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence (jq over 8ba3527f-...jsonl): `Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming`, `Bash ls -la && git log`, `Read .../index.html`, then 5x `AskUserQuestion`. No Write or Edit entries at all. (Skill id is `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, not `superpowers:brainstorming` — plugin appears renamed in this build.)

Five AskUserQuestion tool calls in the log, e.g. on-screen "What already exists that I can't see from this repo?", "Will the first real version of this app have multiple people sharing tasks?", "How should reminders reach you?" — each with a stated recommendation and tradeoffs. Counted in the agent's favor.
